title: T1-T12 ROM after median sternotomy closed with steel wire cerclage (Liebsch 2017 ESJ)
subcategory: long segment with rib cage, sternotomy and closure

quantity.name: ROM
quantity.definition: full range (both directions) T1 vs T12 at +/-2 Nm, last of 3.5 cycles

source.authors: Liebsch C, Graf N, Wilke HJ
source.sample: 6 human C7-L1 thoracic spines with entire rib cage (same 6 specimens as Liebsch 2017 PLoS One)

protocol.summary: C7-L1 with rib cage, C7/L1 potted (C7-T1 screwed), L1 flange 20/30 deg; pure moments +/-2 Nm FE/LB/AR at C7, 1 deg/s (AR 0.5 deg/s), 3.5 cycles, no preload. Steps: baseline, longitudinal median sternotomy, closure with 1.0 mm steel wire (peristernal at upper four intercostal spaces + transsternal above and below lowest peristernal wire).
how_to_simulate: Model C7-L1 with ribs, costal cartilage, split sternum; intercostal muscles absent
Tie the sternal halves with wire cerclage (peristernal intercostal spaces 1-4, two transsternal)
Apply +/-2 Nm pure moments at C7 (L1 fixed), no preload; report T1-T12 full-range ROM and NZ
protocol.notes: ESJ 'intact' ROM/NZ (11.8+/-5.0, 18.3+/-5.4, 25.0+/-9.5; NZ 8.9, 15.3, 3.0) and 'median sternotomy' values are identical to Liebsch 2017 PLoS One 'W/o IM' and 'MST' rows -> same specimens and same measurements; ESJ baseline therefore corresponds to the rib cage WITHOUT intercostal muscles. Only the new wire-cerclage step is written as a test.

extraction.uncertainty: as printed (0.1 deg); '?' in text layer = '+'
extraction.check_notes: Values re-read from text layer; signs '?' interpreted as '+' (consistent with Results text +12 %, +22 %, +8 %, -12 %).

ribcage.intact_structures: ribs, costal cartilage, costovertebral joints; sternum split and re-fixed with wire cerclage; intercostal muscles removed (inferred from identical baseline data with Liebsch 2017 W/o IM)

loading.rate: 1.0 deg/s FE and LB, 0.5 deg/s AR
loading.branch: maximum deflection at +/-2 Nm, last cycle

sequence: intact (as tested here; numerically = Liebsch 2017 'without intercostal muscles')
